validityIssues.evidence: The blank replaces the ENTIRE source sentence 'Garcia was hoping to find the perfect clothing for the performance.' (subject + 'was hoping to' included), but all five options are bare base-form verb phrases ('avoid wearing...', 'perform...', 'seek...'). Inserting the declared answer yields '...sister university in Singapore. Seek an ideal visual presentation for his upcoming stage. That was why he had asked Jeff...' — a subjectless fragment (reads as an imperative inside a third-person narrative). No option produces a grammatical completed sentence. The blank should have been rendered as 'Garcia was hoping to _____.' to match the VP-form options.

Even under the charitable reading 'Garcia was hoping to [option]', answer (5) gives 'hoping to seek an ideal visual presentation', where 'hope to seek' is a stacked-desiderative collocation that is awkward; the source verb was 'find'. Secondary to the fragment defect above.

optionAudit.label: ①
optionAudit.intent: False-consistency trap built from the shopping scene (Jeff choosing white shirt / black jeans over colorful clothes), suggesting Garcia's goal was casual style.
optionAudit.temptingBecause: It is the only other clothing-related option, and the passage does show colorful clothes being rejected in favor of plainer ones.
optionAudit.decisiveFlaw: Polarity/goal error: Garcia's motive was to look right FOR a stage performance, not to avoid formal attire; nothing in the text frames the goal as maintaining a casual style, and it cannot license 'That was why he had asked Jeff to help him pick out new clothes' as a clothing-seeking motive.

optionAudit.label: ②
optionAudit.intent: Surface word-association combo of 'Singapore(an) students' + 'perform' (the item's own explanation admits it is a random association, i.e. filler).
optionAudit.temptingBecause: Reuses salient proper-noun vocabulary ('Singaporean') and the performance theme from the opening sentences.
optionAudit.decisiveFlaw: Actor/relation swap: the band performs FOR the welcoming ceremony honoring the Singaporean students, not WITH them; and it provides no causal link to asking Jeff to pick out clothes.

optionAudit.label: ③
optionAudit.intent: Causal distortion splicing Jeff's lateness (mall scene) onto the rehearsal event.
optionAudit.temptingBecause: 'Late' and 'rehearsal' both literally occur in the passage.
optionAudit.decisiveFlaw: Attribution error: it was Jeff who was late to the mall, not Garcia to any rehearsal; punctuality has no causal connection to requesting help choosing clothes.

optionAudit.label: ④
optionAudit.intent: Anachronistic combo of later-passage vocabulary (nervousness at rehearsal, flawless performance).
optionAudit.temptingBecause: Both 'nervousness' and 'flawless' appear verbatim later in the passage.
optionAudit.decisiveFlaw: Timeline violation: at the blank position Garcia has not yet felt any nervousness (it arises only at the rehearsal), and hiding nervousness cannot explain the clothes-shopping request in the next sentence.

optionAudit.label: ⑤
optionAudit.intent: Declared answer: abstracting paraphrase of the removed span 'find the perfect clothing for the performance' → 'seek an ideal visual presentation for his upcoming stage'.
optionAudit.temptingBecause: Uniquely coheres with the cataphoric causal anchor 'That was why he had asked Jeff to help him pick out new clothes' and with the entire shopping scene.
optionAudit.decisiveFlaw: None semantically (uniquely correct); however, as rendered it produces a subjectless fragment when inserted into the sentence-sized blank (V3 failure shared by all options).

explanationIssues.evidence: The rationale for ② openly states it was generated by '개별 단어를 무작위로 연합하여 생성한 함정 선지' (random word association) — an admission that the distractor lacks a designed misconception, undermining C2 and the KILLER distractor-trap requirement.

The explanation analyzes the blank as 'the third sentence' but never registers that the options are verb phrases while the blank consumes a full sentence including its subject, so the described completion is never actually grammatical.

killerConditionNotes.sameSyntacticSlot: Fails in effect: all five options occupy the same VP slot relative to each other, but none fits the actual sentence-sized blank — every completion is a fragment (§D condition 1 requires grammatical completed sentences).
killerConditionNotes.meaningPreservingAbstraction: Passes: 'ideal visual presentation for his upcoming stage' is a faithful abstraction of 'perfect clothing for the performance'.
killerConditionNotes.anchorOverlapFlawPerDistractor: Fails for ② and ④: both are admitted/apparent random vocabulary combos rather than designed single-decisive-flaw traps.
killerConditionNotes.multiCueRequirement: Fails: the answer is fully determined by the single adjacent sentence 'That was why he had asked Jeff to help him pick out new clothes' — a one-clue local lookup, not a two-sentence/two-cue integration.
killerConditionNotes.noSurfaceGuessing: Fails: ⑤ is the only option about visual appearance for the stage besides the weakly related ①, so clothing-topic matching alone selects it.

notes: V1 verified by byte-level reconstruction: substituting the removed sentence back into the render reproduces the original exactly; single blank marker; labels ①–⑤ consistent across options, answer, wrong-answer explanations, and keyPoints (V5 pass). V2 passes semantically: only ⑤ satisfies the cataphoric causal anchor; each other option has an independent decisive flaw. The fatal defect is the blank seam (V3): a full-sentence blank paired with bare-VP options makes every completed passage ungrammatical. Craft is also far below the requested KILLER band: a light narrative (43–45-style story text) is a weak genre for blank inference, the answer is a one-line local lookup (C5=0), two of four distractors are word-salad fillers (C3=1), and the explanation, while factually accurate (V4 pass), is verbose and self-undermining (C6=2). Repair path: re-render the blank as 'Garcia was hoping to _____.' and replace ②/④ with designed traps (e.g., scope shift on 'performance quality vs appearance', condition-loss on 'for the ceremony'), then re-evaluate difficulty honestly as MID at best.
